  Readable gloss: "The personal name meaning 'God strengthens,' most famously borne by the priest-prophet Ezekiel son of Buzi, who prophesied during the Babylonian exile (Ezekiel 1:3; 24:24). The name also appears in 1 Chronicles 24:16 for a priest assigned to the 19th (or 20th, according to some Greek manuscripts) course in David's organization of temple service. The Greek rendering Ιεζεκιηλ became the standard form in Christian tradition. The theophoric element אל (El, God) combined with חזק (strengthen) creates a name that embodies divine empowerment."

The variants (Yechezqel/Yejezkel) reflect different transliteration traditions.
